defect_observations.observation: Locator precision: the citation [lems 4.6.5-6, thm 4.6.7] directly follows the identification X_inf=E(Z|F_inf); in the held source that identification is the content of Thm 4.6.8 and its proof (p.247), not of the cited lemmas/theorem. The source does support the claim, so no verdict change.

The finite-dimensional coordinatewise extension and the no-uncountable-interchange sentence sit before the thm 4.7.3 citation, but the held source p.250 has no vector extension (a handbook addition carried by the source cite through its placement). The annex (633-641) argues the extension for the scalar upward/downward theorems, i.e. statements about one integrable vector, which is how the body sentence words it.

The definition restricts uniform integrability to families of integrable variables. The held source (p.244) defines it for any collection and derives sup E|X_i|<=M+1. Consequently C003 (body 49-51, annex 36-44) never states that sup E Phi(|X_i|)<inf by itself forces integrability, as source Thm 4.6.2 gives for arbitrary families. This is a one-line consequence of the annex display, so no verdict change.

No inline locator for Durrett Thm 4.6.2 (the annex at line 44 says 'the source criterion'), and C007 (body 110-121) has none for Thm 4.6.4. Only the chapter-level cite at body line 10 (pp. 244-250) covers them. The content matches the held source pp.245-246.

The completed-Lebesgue transfer lists integrability, cell integrals and L1 approximation but does not state the almost-everywhere convergence transfer explicitly. That transfer is immediate from the Borel version g=f a.e. with identical cell averages.
The body asserts |Y|<=Z a.s. and no annex line states it. It is the a.s. limit of |Y_n|<=Z, which the annex uses implicitly (318-319).

The closing paragraph delegates Section 4.7 applications and exercises to sec:p15-exchangeability-and-definetti and to P17 theorems; the labels exist on the route. This lies outside the 21 owed components and was not assessed.
